commits.message:
A transition, a spinner and a WidgetApp view pass the edge; an effect and a renderable print do not change it (rich-control-codes-xh4n.5ya)

Second high review of #584. Recolored and Reglyphed drop the mark so an
effect never sees a right-to-left text's pad cells; a printed renderable's
rows are closed lines whatever its end.

Animations, effects, function views and print fragments pass the edge as text does (rich-control-codes-xh4n.5ya)

Medium review of #584. The mark stays opt-in: a pass-through that misses it
leaves text unplaced (master's behavior), where a missed opt-out moves a
layout. The mark is a prototype getter; passingOptions returns the options
unchanged unless it drops a default.

The filled-row default edge reaches text and what passes options on, not every renderable (rich-control-codes-xh4n.5ya)

Review of #584: opt-out justify "default" moved Pretty, JSON, Align and a
Traceback's message. PASSES_EDGE in core/protocol marks RichText,
EmbeddedText, Group and Constrain; renderFilling starts the default, renderPassing
forwards it, and anything unmarked loses only the default. besideDrawing removed.

Right-to-left text through a Group, a Viewport, a scroll or a view stands at its start edge (rich-control-codes-xh4n.5ya)

Every row-filling container hands its body justify "default", not only a
text body: Padding, Layout, Viewport, scroll, Console.print's renderable
blocks and drawView (Live, App). Group and Constrain forward it. A Tree
label and a traceback frame sit beside other drawing, so they drop only
the default (besideDrawing) and keep a justify the print named.
Left-to-right output is unchanged: RichText alone reads justify, and
"default" draws a left-to-right row as no justify does.

A stated component text is held on its ground, opaque or tint (rich-unfiled-791c.h35m) (#585)

* A stated component text is held on its ground, opaque or tint: an author's color that reads is kept, one that does not keeps its hue (rich-unfiled-791c.h35m)

* A footer key's text is held on the footer bar its ground sits on; buildPalette's contract names held component text (rich-unfiled-791c.h35m)

* A stated component text is held on its own side of its ground, on the footer item a footer key sits on; contrast page says so (rich-unfiled-791c.h35m)

* A held component text that must cross its ground keeps its hue (rich-unfiled-791c.h35m)
